sections.heading: C — Parking, Stopping, or Standing
sections.markdown:
## C — Parking, Stopping, or Standing

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
Parked cars can still cause crashes, so drivers kill the motor, set the brake, pocket the key, and check behind for traffic before swinging doors open [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Nothing may park, stop, or stand idling roadside of a parked car, on sidewalks or crosswalks, inside intersections, between safety zones and curbs or within thirty feet opposite their ends, beside excavations that block traffic, on bridges, elevated spans, tunnels, rails, or where signs ban stopping [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
Occupied or not, vehicles never park or stand ahead of driveways, within fifteen feet of hydrants, within twenty feet of intersection crosswalks, within thirty feet before roadside signals and signs, within twenty feet of fire-station doors or seventy-five feet across from them, or where signs ban parking or standing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
Parking alone is further banned within fifty feet of rails and where signs ban it, rural highways demand off-road parking or else passing room plus two-hundred-foot visibility both ways with night lights or dim headlamps, and bicycles may rest on sidewalks that stay passable [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
Disabled-space abuse is a misdemeanor fining five hundred to seven hundred fifty dollars first and climbing to one thousand two hundred fifty dollars plus community service by the fifth offense, while obedience stops for signs and signals never count as parking or standing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A02
Disabled spaces need plates or removable windshield cards used only while carrying the holder, cards stay unlent, ramps stay unblocked, counterfeits and alterations stay criminal, some cities also ban stopping or standing there, and striped lift zones stay empty [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A02
Unattended idling breaks the law without engine-off, locked ignition, removed key, set brake, and grade-parked wheels to the curb, though remote starters skip the key rules until a key rides along to drive [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A02
Parallel parking starts with a roomy space, an early signal, and a stop even with the lead car two feet out, then hard-right wheels backing curbward clear of oncoming cars, while two-way streets park right wheels within eighteen inches of the curb [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A03
Parallel finishes swing hard left once seats meet bumpers, back to six inches from the curb and never beyond eighteen, then straighten centered in the space [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A03
Hill parking aims wheels curbward with or without curbs as diagrammed, departures check mirrors and backs for children between cars with exit signals, residential drivers watch for children, and downhill neutral coasting stays illegal [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0050]

items.why: Section Seven is rule-and-distance recall served by standard flashcards and quizzes; no separate practice mode is needed.

corpus_stability.reason: The Texas Driver Handbook is a periodically revised official edition, so Section Seven parking rules change at most with new editions.
